standard_prerequisites.name: Omega-consistency
standard_prerequisites.statement: A theory is omega-inconsistent when for some formula A(x) it proves the existential 'there is x with A(x)' while also proving each negated instance A(n-bar); omega-consistent theories are consistent.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof concludes by displaying exactly this pattern for the proof predicate (536-541).

standard_prerequisites.name: The Godel sentence and its Q-form
standard_prerequisites.statement: The negated Godel sentence is equivalent in Q to the existential 'there is x with Prf_T(x, gG_T)' (the unit's equation eqn:qpf).
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the assumed derivation of the negated Godel sentence into a derivation of the existential (538-540).

standard_prerequisites.name: Consistent theories do not prove the Godel sentence
standard_prerequisites.statement: If T is consistent then T does not derive G_T; the unit proves this as its own lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies, in the consistent case, the non-derivability from which the numeral instances are refuted (528-531).

standard_prerequisites.name: Representability of the proof predicate in Q
standard_prerequisites.statement: For each n, the fact that there is no derivation of a given sentence coded n is witnessed in Q by a derivation of the negated proof predicate instance Prf_T(n-bar, gG_T); this representability standard of the unit underwrites the infinite family.
standard_prerequisites.use: It yields the displayed family of Q-derivations, hence T-derivations, of every negated numeral instance (531-537).

core_obligations: Assume T derives the negation of its Godel sentence; if T is inconsistent it is omega-inconsistent outright (524-527).
Otherwise T is consistent, so by the unit's unprovability lemma T does not derive G_T (528-531).
From the non-derivability of G_T, representability of the proof predicate in Q gives derivations in Q, hence in T, of the negation of Prf_T(n-bar, gG_T) for every n (531-537).

By the Q-equivalence of the negated Godel sentence with the existential over the proof predicate, T also derives that existential; the pattern makes T omega-inconsistent, so the assumption is refuted (538-541).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the contraposition and dispatch the inconsistent case.
Produce the infinite family of refuted numeral instances from non-derivability of the Godel sentence.
Contrast with the existential form and conclude omega-inconsistency.

difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 517-520: an omega-consistent axiomatizable theory extending Q does not prove the negation of its Godel sentence. The author proof (522-541) runs a genuine omega-inconsistency construction: assuming T proves the negation of G_T, it splits on consistency, invokes the unit's unprovability lemma in the consistent case, produces the infinite family of refutations of each numeral instance of the proof predicate from the non-derivability of G_T, and contrasts this with the existential form of the negated Godel sentence supplied by the unit's Q-equivalence, landing exactly on omega-inconsistency. Keeping the infinitude of the numeral instances and the single existential aligned is the load-bearing move.
